papers.title: PIMENTO: A primer inference toolkit to facilitate large-scale calling of amplicon sequence variants.
papers.abstract: The identification of amplicon sequence variants from DNA metabarcoding data is a common method for revealing the taxonomic makeup of environmental samples, and for allowing comparative studies between similar datasets. A significant hurdle to the large-scale calling of amplicon sequence variants from publicly available nucleotide datasets is the heterogeneous presence of primer sequences in reads, the removal of which is a necessary pre-processing step for this form of analysis. Furthermore, as the details of the experimental primers are rarely captured in the metadata associated with the seq
papers.summary: PIMENTO is a new bioinformatics toolkit that automates the detection and removal of primer sequences from DNA metabarcoding reads, addressing a major bottleneck in large-scale amplicon sequence variant (ASV) calling. By inferring primers directly from the data, it enables more efficient and reproducible processing of publicly available nucleotide datasets for taxonomic and comparative studies.

papers.title: Non-pharmacological interventions for lactational mastitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
papers.abstract: Lactational mastitis is a common inflammatory condition that can adversely affect maternal well-being and is associated with early cessation of breastfeeding. Although antibiotics and analgesics are widely used in clinical practice, concerns regarding antimicrobial resistance and potential effects on the infant microbiome have prompted increasing interest in non-pharmacological approaches. A range of physical and biological interventions, including probiotics, therapeutic ultrasound, acupuncture and manual therapies, have been investigated; however, the comparative effectiveness and safety of
papers.summary: This protocol outlines a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate non-pharmacological interventions for lactational mastitis, such as probiotics, ultrasound, and acupuncture. The study aims to compare their effectiveness and safety, addressing growing concerns about antibiotic use and its impact on the infant microbiome.

papers.title: CAMEO: a CAZyme mapping engine optimized for HUMAnN.
papers.abstract: There are technical barriers to creating functional mapping databases and a dearth of validated databases that can be easily implemented by users. We present CAMEO, a precomputed and validated mapping file for carbohydrate-active enzymes, as well as an approach to building new CAZyme mapping files, for use with HUMAnN.
papers.summary: CAMEO provides a precomputed, validated mapping file for carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) that works with the HUMAnN functional profiling tool, along with a method to build custom CAZyme mapping files. This addresses the lack of easily usable CAZyme databases for metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analysis.

papers.title: Viruses help shape microbiome response to polyphenol rewiring of methane-suppressed peat microcosms.
papers.abstract: Human activities are accelerating permafrost thaw and subsequent methane emissions from increased microbial activity, prompting microbiome engineering efforts as an emissions mitigation strategy. We recently demonstrated that catechin amendment could drastically reduce methane emissions (>80%) in peat microcosms by enriching catechin-degrading prokaryotes that outcompeted methanogens for hydrogen. However, viral contributions to such microbiome-level responses remain unexplored and we hypothesized that viral dynamics could help shape the microbiome response as nutrient amendments may alter cel
papers.summary: This study investigates how viruses influence the microbiome's response to polyphenol (catechin) amendment in peat microcosms, a strategy previously shown to reduce methane emissions. The authors find that viral dynamics, including changes in viral abundance and host interactions, help shape the prokaryotic community restructuring that leads to methane suppression, highlighting a previously overlooked role for viruses in microbiome engineering outcomes.

papers.title: Bacterial-based cancer therapy: mechanisms and therapeutic advances.
papers.abstract: Targeted cancer therapies increasingly require platforms that can penetrate poorly perfused tumor regions while minimizing systemic toxicity. Bacteria, owing to their intrinsic tumor tropism, genetic programmability, and immunostimulatory properties, have re-emerged as versatile anticancer agents, ranging from attenuated tumor-colonizing strains to highly engineered "living therapeutics." In this review, we synthesize the mechanistic foundations and therapeutic advances of bacterial-based cancer therapy through four major themes. First, we examine foundational mechanisms, including tumor-selec
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the mechanistic foundations and therapeutic advances of bacterial-based cancer therapy, highlighting bacteria's intrinsic tumor tropism, genetic programmability, and immunostimulatory properties. It covers foundational mechanisms and the development of engineered 'living therapeutics' as versatile anticancer agents.

papers.title: Nanopore sequencing reveals coordinated host and microbiome responses across barley genotypes.
papers.abstract: Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) provides a suitable model for studying domestication-driven plant-microbiome interactions. Although wild, landrace, and modern genotypes host distinct rhizosphere communities, the extent to which roots and microbes reciprocally influence each other remains unclear. Here, we applied an integrated multi-omics approach combining long-read metagenomics, root transcriptomics, and plant genomics to understand genotype-specific host-microbiome coordination.
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated multi-omics approach combining long-read metagenomics, root transcriptomics, and plant genomics to investigate how different barley genotypes (wild, landrace, and modern) coordinate with their rhizosphere microbiomes. The findings reveal genotype-specific host-microbiome interactions, providing insights into domestication-driven changes in plant-microbe relationships.

papers.title: Evolution of the fecal and oral microbiota after prophylactic antibiotics administered for dental surgeries.
papers.abstract: The human oral and gut microbiomes play critical roles in maintaining overall health. Although systemic antibiotics are frequently prescribed perioperatively in dental procedures, their impact on microbiota composition and diversity remains inadequately understood. The authors' objective was to characterize the evolution of the gut and oral microbiomes after a course of antibiotics administered for dental surgeries. The authors hypothesized that the microbiome would experience disruption but eventually recover to baseline levels and that patient-related factors would influence the extent of di
papers.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
papers.summary: This study characterizes how a course of prophylactic antibiotics for dental surgeries affects the gut and oral microbiomes over time, testing whether microbial communities recover to baseline and whether patient factors influence the degree of disruption. The findings provide insights into the resilience of the human microbiome after antibiotic exposure in a common clinical setting.

papers.title: The Gut-brain-adipose Axis in Ultra-processed Food and Obesity: A Mechanistic Synthesis and Its Implications for Food Classification.
papers.abstract: Consumption of ultra-processed food (UPF) tracks closely with obesity across populations, and the Nova classification has become the dominant tool for capturing that exposure. Why UPF promotes weight gain is a separate question, and the biological answer has accumulated in fragments. I draw those strands together and ask whether three mechanisms usually studied in isolation: gut microbial disruption, hypothalamic inflammation, and adipose tissue dysfunction, are better understood as one connected system, and what that would mean for how UPF is classified.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence linking ultra-processed food consumption to obesity through three interconnected mechanisms: gut microbial disruption, hypothalamic inflammation, and adipose tissue dysfunction, proposing they operate as a unified gut-brain-adipose axis. The author argues that recognizing this integrated system could inform more biologically meaningful food classification beyond the current Nova system.

papers.title: Innovative Test Strip-Based Colorimetric Sensors Integrated With Affinity Chromatography: Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitor Screening Breakthrough in Lycium Barbarum Leaves.
papers.abstract: Current Alzheimer's drugs exhibit limited effectiveness, highlighting the necessity for multi-target treatments. This study developed an innovative and efficient screening platform combining hydrogen peroxide test strip-based colorimetric sensing with affinity chromatography for rapid identification of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors from complex herbal medicines. Applying this strategy, from Lycium barbarum leaves, we identified three potent inhibitors: chlorogenic acid, N-acetyl-N'-caffeoylputrescine (NANCP), and N-caffeoylputrescine (NCP), with IC50 ranging from 55.7 to 143.2 µm. Mol
papers.summary: This study presents a new screening platform that combines hydrogen peroxide test strip-based colorimetric sensing with affinity chromatography to rapidly identify acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors from complex herbal mixtures. Using this method, the authors discovered three potent AChE inhibitors from Lycium barbarum leaves, with IC50 values in the micromolar range, offering a potential multi-target approach for Alzheimer's disease treatment.

papers.title: Wastewater-based human gut microbiome surveillance links microbial signatures to population health in Ohio communities.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has been widely used to track infectious diseases, yet its potential for population-level gut microbiome surveillance and broader public health assessment remains limited. Here, we present a multi-city study in Ohio, USA, demonstrating how sewage-derived human gut microbiome profiles can be leveraged to infer community health patterns. In this retrospective cross-sectional study, influent wastewater samples were collected from eight Ohio cities (May - June 2022). Community-level gut bacterial profiles were characterized and integrated with publicly available
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that wastewater-based epidemiology can be extended beyond infectious disease tracking to surveil population-level gut microbiome signatures, revealing associations with community health indicators across eight Ohio cities. The findings suggest sewage-derived microbial profiles could serve as a non-invasive tool for public health assessment.

papers.title: Strain-level ecological filtering governs microbial colonization of the human gut.
papers.abstract: Microbial colonization of the human gut is typically inferred from species-level profiling, yet durable establishment operates at the strain level. Here, using longitudinal shotgun metagenomics across multiple donor-recipient pairs undergoing fecal microbiota transplantation, we show that colonization is governed by lineage-dependent strain-level ecological filtering. Strain-resolved analyses reveal that gut colonization imposes reproducible population-genetic bottlenecks, characterized by reduced nucleotide diversity and selective strain capture. Lineage identity is the primary determinant of
papers.summary: This study uses longitudinal shotgun metagenomics from fecal microbiota transplant recipients to show that gut colonization is governed by strain-level ecological filtering, not just species-level dynamics. The authors find reproducible population-genetic bottlenecks with reduced nucleotide diversity and selective strain capture, where lineage identity is the primary determinant of successful colonization.

papers.title: Assessing the Relationship between Gut Microbiota and Kidney Stones: A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Analysis.
papers.abstract: There is increasing evidence that gut microbiota is associated with the risk of kidney stones diseases (KSD), but whether a causal relationship exists remains unclear. We used the Mendelian randomization (MR) method to assess the potential causal relationship between gut microbiota and KSD risk.
papers.summary: This study uses two-sample Mendelian randomization to investigate whether gut microbiota composition has a causal effect on kidney stone disease risk. The findings provide evidence for a potential causal relationship between certain gut microbes and kidney stones, though the specific taxa and direction of effect are not detailed in the abstract.

papers.title: Short communication: Oral microbiome as a potential proxy for methane emissions in grazing tropical composite beef cattle.
papers.abstract: Enteric methane emissions from ruminant livestock contribute to global warming, creating an urgent need for effective mitigation strategies that do not compromise animal productivity and welfare. Methanogenic archaea within the rumen microbiome drive enteric methane emissions. However, large-scale rumen-fluid sampling in commercial production systems is impractical, due to its invasive nature and the associated logistical challenges. This study hypothesised that rumination facilitates the capture of rumen microbial signals within the oral cavity, therefore oral microbiome profiles can be a pra
papers.summary: This study investigates whether oral microbiome samples can serve as a non-invasive proxy for methane emissions in grazing beef cattle, given the impracticality of rumen fluid sampling in commercial settings. The findings suggest that oral microbial profiles may reflect rumen methanogen signals, offering a potential alternative for large-scale methane monitoring.

papers.title: Comparative metagenomic assessment of Illumina-compatible library preparation methods, short-read lengths, and PacBio HiFi sequencing reveals differences in microbial and functional diversity recovery from a complex environmental sample.
papers.abstract: Metagenomics enables comprehensive exploration of microbial communities but is influenced by library preparation and sequencing technologies, affecting recovery of microbial genomes and proteins. Here, we benchmarked six Illumina-compatible short-read library preparation conditions in triplicate at 2 × 150 bp and 2 × 250 bp read lengths alongside PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing using a composite environmental sample of marine mangrove sediment and terrestrial palm tree soil. Longer short reads (2 × 250 bp) combined with optimal library preparation approaches improved assembly quality, protein
papers.summary: This study benchmarks different library preparation methods and sequencing platforms (Illumina short-read vs. PacBio HiFi long-read) on a complex environmental sample, showing that longer short reads (2x250 bp) with optimal library prep improve assembly quality and protein recovery, while HiFi sequencing offers advantages for certain analyses. The findings provide practical guidance for maximizing microbial and functional diversity recovery in metagenomic studies.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Microbial Gene Catalog of the Human Airway Microbiome Across Anatomical Sites and Geographic Regions.
papers.abstract: The respiratory microbiota is a critical determinant of airway health, yet functional characterization remains challenging due to the lack of a high-resolution reference catalog. To address this gap and enable systematic investigation at both species and gene levels, we constructed the integrated Human Airway Microbiome Gene Catalog (iHAMGC) through high-throughput metagenomic analysis of 12,273 airway samples. This catalog comprises 24,185,985 non-redundant microbial genes and provides extensive taxonomic and functional annotations, with a particular focus on clinically relevant elements, inc
papers.summary: This paper presents the integrated Human Airway Microbiome Gene Catalog (iHAMGC), a comprehensive reference of over 24 million non-redundant microbial genes derived from 12,273 airway samples across anatomical sites and geographic regions. The catalog provides extensive taxonomic and functional annotations, with emphasis on clinically relevant elements, enabling systematic investigation of the respiratory microbiome at both species and gene levels.

papers.title: Lachnospiraceae and Its Metabolite Malate Act in Concert to Repair Gut Microbiota Imbalance and Block Colorectal Cancer Progression.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis is a crucial driver of the initiation and progression of colorectal cancer (CRC), where functional gut microbes and their metabolites play key roles in the microecological regulation of CRC. Currently, the association between Lachnospiraceae and CRC progression, as well as the underlying mechanisms, remains incompletely understood and warrants further investigation.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of Lachnospiraceae and its metabolite malate in colorectal cancer (CRC), finding that they work together to repair gut microbiota imbalance and block CRC progression. The findings suggest a potential therapeutic avenue for CRC through modulation of gut microbiota and metabolite supplementation.

papers.title: [Optimization of the enzymatic hydrolysis process of β-agarase Y3R1 from Catenovulum agarivorans and effects of the products on intestinal microbiota during in vitro fermentation].
papers.abstract: This study aimed to optimize the hydrolysis conditions of agarose by β-agarase Y3R1 and to investigate the prebiotic effects of its product, neoagarooligosaccharides, on gut microbiota. Using reducing sugar yield as the evaluation index, the enzymatic hydrolysis process of β-agarase Y3R1 from Catenovellum agarivorans was optimized. The content of reducing sugar and total sugar generated during the reaction were determined via the 3,5-dinitrosalicylic acid (DNS) method and the phenol-sulfuric acid method, respectively, and the average degree of polymerization (DP) of the enzymatic hydrolysis pr
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study optimized the enzymatic hydrolysis of agarose by β-agarase Y3R1 from Catenovulum agarivorans to produce neoagarooligosaccharides, and evaluated their prebiotic effects on gut microbiota during in vitro fermentation. The optimized process improved reducing sugar yield, and the resulting oligosaccharides modulated intestinal microbiota composition, suggesting potential as functional prebiotics.

papers.title: MeioBIOME: A snakemake workflow for the parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and host-associated bacteria/archaea.
papers.abstract: Microbes closely interact with every living organism, including meiofauna (i.e., microbial eukaryotes 38 μm - 1 mm in length), and influence the development, life cycle, and evolution of diverse metazoans. Together, meiofauna and their microbiomes, collectively referred to as the holobiont, underpin biogeochemical cycles and drive decomposition of organic matter. However, our understanding of the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of meiofauna microbiomes are limited, typically owed to low-resolution 16S rRNA surveys, which cannot accurately delineate bacterial taxa. Single-specimen holobion
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MeioBIOME is a new Snakemake workflow that enables parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and their associated bacteria/archaea from single-specimen holobiont samples. It addresses the limitations of low-resolution 16S rRNA surveys by providing a scalable, reproducible pipeline for high-resolution genomic and metagenomic analysis, which could improve understanding of meiofauna-microbiome interactions and their ecological roles.

papers.title: Taxonomic and Functional Comparative Metagenomics of Peruvian Salterns: Insights into Microbial Communities and Aminotransferase Potential.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic analysis of extreme environments is essential in biotechnological research. This work aimed to determine and compare the microbial diversity of two Peruvian saline environments and characterise their functional profiles. Soil metagenomic DNA (mDNA) was analysed from Maras and Pilluana salterns, both with a thalassohaline origin but with different geographical and environmental conditions. Maras samples exhibited more diversity and a remarkably higher abundance of archaea (phylum Euryarchaeota). The most dominant bacterial phyla across all the samples were Pseudomonadota and Actinom
papers.summary: This study compares the microbial diversity and functional potential of two Peruvian salterns (Maras and Pilluana) using metagenomics, revealing that Maras has higher diversity and a greater abundance of archaea, while both sites are dominated by bacterial phyla such as Pseudomonadota and Actinobacteria. The research also explores aminotransferase potential, highlighting biotechnological applications of extremophilic microbes.

papers.title: Pine-Extracted Volatile Oils Suppress Root Rot in Psammosilene tunicoides Through Direct Antifungal Activity and Rhizosphere Microbiome Modulation.
papers.abstract: Frequent outbreaks of root rot in Psammosilene tunicoides W. C. Wu & C. Y. Wu severely compromise the quality of its medicinal materials and hinder its large-scale cultivation. Interestingly, wild P. tunicoides growing under pine trees rarely experience this disease. To explore the potential basis of root rot suppression, we evaluated the direct antifungal activity of pine-derived volatile oils and the associated changes in the rhizosphere microbiome. GC-MS showed that pine turpentine was dominated by α-pinene (45.50%) and longifolene (28.20%). In vitro assays confirmed its highly efficient in
papers.summary: This study investigates why wild Psammosilene tunicoides growing under pine trees rarely suffer from root rot, finding that pine-derived volatile oils (dominated by α-pinene and longifolene) directly inhibit fungal pathogens and also modulate the rhizosphere microbiome to suppress disease. The results suggest a dual mechanism—direct antifungal activity plus beneficial microbiome shifts—that could inform sustainable disease management for this medicinal plant.

papers.title: Changes in the Gut Microbiome Following Perioperative Prophylactic Cefazolin Administration in Patients Undergoing Orthopedic Surgery: A Longitudinal Prospective Study.
papers.abstract: Cefazolin is a first-generation cephalosporin with a moderate antimicrobial spectrum and the ability to induce the production of beta-lactamases by bacterial hosts. We investigated the effect of prophylactic cefazolin administration on the gut microbiome in patients undergoing orthopedic surgery.
papers.summary: This longitudinal prospective study examined how prophylactic cefazolin, a common antibiotic used in orthopedic surgery, affects the gut microbiome of patients. The findings reveal changes in gut microbial composition following cefazolin administration, highlighting potential impacts of routine surgical prophylaxis on the microbiome.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Viral Communities in Hospital, University and Urban Wastewater by Shotgun Metagenomic Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance has emerged as a powerful approach for population-level monitoring of pathogen circulation in a timely and non-invasive manner. In this study, shotgun metagenomic sequencing was applied to wastewater samples collected from a hospital (HP), a university campus (UN), and a wastewater treatment plant (WTP). Viral sequences were taxonomically classified using Kraken2. Specifically, HP samples showed the highest viral richness, followed by WTP and UN samples (HP vs. UN, p = 0.0003; WTP vs. UN, p = 0.0018). Using Jaccard distance, significant differences were observed b
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare viral communities in wastewater from a hospital, a university campus, and a wastewater treatment plant. Hospital samples showed the highest viral richness, and significant differences in viral community composition were observed between sites, highlighting the utility of wastewater-based surveillance for tracking pathogens across different population settings.

papers.title: Composting Restructures Chicken Manure Viral Communities and Attenuates Virus-Associated Antibiotic Resistance Signals: Paired Metagenome and Virome Analyses.
papers.abstract: Composting is widely used to reduce biological risks during manure recycling, but changes in viral communities and virus-associated antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) remain poorly resolved. This study aimed to assess changes in DNA viral communities, eukaryotic viral protein signals, virus-associated ARGs, and predicted virus-host linkages during chicken manure composting using paired analyses of total-community metagenomes and viral-particle-enriched viromes. Both approaches recovered viral assemblages dominated by Uroviricota and lytic viruses but produced distinct profiles. Viromes yielded
papers.summary: This study used paired metagenomic and viromic approaches to show that composting significantly restructures the viral communities in chicken manure, reducing the abundance of virus-associated antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). The findings highlight composting as an effective method to attenuate viral contributions to antibiotic resistance spread in agricultural waste.

papers.title: Cold Exposure Shifts Gut Microbial Butyrate Synthesis Toward the Lysine-Dependent and But-Mediated Terminal Pathways to Enhance Cold Tolerance in Min Pigs.
papers.abstract: This study combined seasonal observation in Min pigs and acute cold challenge experiments in Min pigs and Large White pigs to analyze changes in gut butyrate synthesis under cold exposure and its association with thermogenesis. Compared with summer, Min pigs in winter showed significantly higher Bacteroidota abundance (p = 0.006), lysine-pathway genes (p < 0.05), and relative gene abundance of the but terminal pathway (p < 0.05). Fecal (47.96 vs. 40.24 µmol/L, p = 0.020) and serum (4.64 vs. 2.17 µmol/L, p = 0.046) butyrate were also elevated and correlated with 10 thermogenesis-related genes (
papers.summary: This study shows that cold exposure in Min pigs shifts gut microbial butyrate production toward the lysine-dependent and But-mediated terminal pathways, increasing fecal and serum butyrate levels that correlate with thermogenesis-related gene expression. These findings suggest a mechanistic link between gut microbiota butyrate synthesis and cold tolerance in pigs.

papers.title: Microbial Inulinases: Characterization, Properties, and Potential Contribution to Metabolic and Nutritional Health.
papers.abstract: Microbial inulinases are enzymes produced by bacteria, yeasts, and fungi that can hydrolyze inulin into fructose and fructooligosaccharides (FOSs). The article discusses the various types of inulinases (exo- and endo-inulinases), microbial sources, biochemical properties, and optimal activity conditions, which are critical for their use in biotechnological and food processes. Special emphasis is placed on inulin degradation products, particularly FOSs, which are known for their prebiotic properties. They promote the growth of beneficial intestinal microbiota, helping to maintain digestive heal
papers.summary: This review characterizes microbial inulinases—enzymes from bacteria, yeasts, and fungi that break down inulin into fructose and prebiotic fructooligosaccharides (FOSs). It covers enzyme types, sources, biochemical properties, and optimal conditions, highlighting the potential health benefits of FOSs in promoting beneficial gut microbiota and digestive health.

papers.title: Host phylogeny and diet shape gut microbiome and virome in wild small mammals of Gongga Mountain, China.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiotas play pivotal roles in host adaptation, yet their composition and function in high-altitude small mammals remain poorly characterized. This study investigated how host phylogeny (order-level) and dietary habits shape the gut microbiome and virome of three mammalian orders (Eulipotyphla, Rodentia, Lagomorpha) in Gongga Mountain, a biodiversity hotspot on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau. Metagenomic sequencing of 219 samples from 22 species revealed order-specific microbial signatures: Eulipotyphla (carnivorous) harbored higher abundances of potential pathogens (e.g., Helicobacter, Haf
papers.summary: This study characterizes the gut microbiome and virome of wild small mammals across three orders in Gongga Mountain, China, using metagenomic sequencing of 219 samples from 22 species. It finds that host phylogeny and diet shape microbial community composition, with carnivorous Eulipotyphla harboring more potential pathogens, providing new insights into high-altitude host-microbe interactions.

papers.title: Antimicrobial peptides in anti-infective and immunomodulatory applications: Mechanisms, challenges, and emerging computational design.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs) evolutionarily conserved effectors of innate immunity, have emerged as multifunctional agents with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, immunomodulatory capabilities, and potential applicability in cancer therapy. Despite their functional diversity and biological potency, the clinical translation of AMPs remains constrained by significant challenges, including proteolytic instability, hemolytic toxicity, high production costs, and protracted development pipelines. This review examines how the diverse molecular mechanisms through which AMPs exert antimicrobial ef
papers.summary: This review covers antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) as multifunctional innate immunity effectors with broad-spectrum antimicrobial, immunomodulatory, and potential anticancer activities, while detailing key clinical translation barriers such as proteolytic instability, hemolytic toxicity, and high production costs. It also highlights emerging computational design approaches to overcome these challenges and accelerate AMP development.

papers.title: Feasibility and Compliance of Stool Collection for Future Microbiome-Based Colorectal Cancer Screening: Preliminary Findings from a Prospective Multicenter FIT-Positive Cohort.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, and early detection through population-based screening programs significantly reduces both incidence and mortality. Although gut microbiome-based biomarkers have emerged as promising non-invasive tools for CRC detection, limited evidence is available regarding patient acceptance and compliance with microbiome-based screening studies, factors that may influence their future implementation in clinical practice. We conducted a preliminary analysis of an ongoing multicenter, prospective observational study designed to develop a gut micr
papers.summary: This preliminary study from a prospective multicenter cohort of FIT-positive patients assesses the feasibility and patient compliance of stool collection for future microbiome-based colorectal cancer screening. The findings provide early evidence on patient acceptance and practical implementation factors that could influence the adoption of microbiome-based screening in clinical practice.

papers.title: Deciphering the Streptococcus mutans essentialome: multi-omic resolution of hypothetical genes and identification of a functional RocS equivalent.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide viability catalogs produced by transposon sequencing (Tn-seq) and CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) have successfully mapped the essential genome of Streptococcus mutans . However, particularly for genes annotated as "hypothetical" or uncharacterized, translating these findings into mechanistic biological functions remains a significant bottleneck. In this study, we developed an integrated functional genomics pipeline combining predictive bioinformatics, tunable CRISPRi transcriptional silencing, transmission electron microscopy, transcriptomics, and genetic suppressor screens to chara
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated functional genomics pipeline to characterize hypothetical genes in the essential genome of Streptococcus mutans, combining CRISPRi silencing, transcriptomics, and suppressor screens. The work identifies a functional equivalent of RocS and provides a multi-omic approach to assign biological functions to uncharacterized essential genes.

papers.title: Phylogenize2: robust phylogenetic methods link genes to phenotypes across host-associated and environmental microbiomes.
papers.abstract: In microbiome studies, associations between microbial functions and the environment are often confounded by phylogeny. While some methods explicitly account for this confounder, they require information about genome content, limiting their use in biomes where few genomes have been available. To make these methods more universally accessible, we have developed Phylogenize2, a redesigned phylogeny-aware tool for linking microbial gene families to abundance phenotypes. Phylogenize2 integrates large metagenome-assembled genome collections, including both biome-specific collections from MGnify and
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Phylogenize2 is a redesigned tool that links microbial gene families to environmental phenotypes while accounting for phylogenetic confounding, now compatible with large metagenome-assembled genome collections from diverse biomes. It makes phylogeny-aware association testing more accessible for host-associated and environmental microbiomes where reference genomes were previously limited.

papers.title: A robust, sensitive phylogenetic method enables gene-level metagenomic analyses.
papers.abstract: A key goal in the microbiome field is to move from taxonomic associations towards mechanistic hypotheses about microbial gene function. However, most methods for linking microbiome changes to specific genes are biased towards finding marker genes, with weak evidence for functional relevance. Phylogenetic regression can address this issue and has been previously applied to changes in microbial prevalence, but many environments (such as the gut in health vs. disease) are characterized more by changes in abundance, which presents unique statistical challenges. We show that when applied to real di
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a robust and sensitive phylogenetic regression method for gene-level metagenomic analysis, addressing the challenge of linking microbiome abundance changes to specific microbial genes. The method overcomes statistical biases toward marker genes and is validated on real gut microbiome data, enabling more reliable identification of functionally relevant genes in health versus disease.

papers.title: Assessment of Stability of Preservation Techniques for Strawberry Soil Microbiomes: Exploring the Biotechnological Relevance for Sustainable Agriculture.
papers.abstract: Preserving ex situ soil microbial communities is essential for bacterial biodiversity conservation in microbiome biobanking, accurate microbiome research, and future biotechnological applications in sustainable agriculture. The effect of three soil preservation methods-cryopreservation at -80 °C, refrigeration at 4 °C, and lyophilization-on the viability, diversity and metabolic functionality of the soil microbiome was evaluated using soil from untreated and solarized strawberry fields stored at 0, 6 and 12 months. Microbial viability, ecological strategies, functionality, and diversity were a
papers.summary: This study evaluates how different soil preservation methods (cryopreservation, refrigeration, and lyophilization) affect the viability, diversity, and metabolic functionality of strawberry soil microbiomes over 12 months. The findings provide practical guidance for microbiome biobanking and highlight the biotechnological relevance of preservation techniques for sustainable agriculture.

papers.title: Evaluating the Effect of Sampling Scale on Mosquito Virome Characterization Using PacBio HiFi Long-Read Metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Characterizing the mosquito virome is essential for understanding host-microbiota interactions and vector competence, but it can be influenced by sample scale, sequencing strategy, and host depletion. This study evaluated the effect of sampling scale on mosquito virome characterization using a third-generation sequencing (TGS) metagenomics approach based on PacBio HiFi long reads, applied to L4 larvae and adults of Aedes mariae, analyzing single individuals and pools of increasing size before and after host genome removal. The results showed that sequencing yield did not increase with pool siz
papers.summary: This study evaluates how sampling scale (single individuals vs. pools of increasing size) affects mosquito virome characterization using PacBio HiFi long-read metagenomics. The findings indicate that sequencing yield did not increase with pool size, providing practical insights for designing virome surveillance studies in mosquitoes.

papers.title: Microbial Community Differentiation and Predicted Chemical-Defense-Related Functional Potential Across Distinct Microhabitats of Cultured Hemicentrotus pulcherrimus.
papers.abstract: Sea urchins harbor diverse microbial communities that may contribute to host-associated ecological interactions, microbial competition, and chemical defense. However, the compartment-specific organization of sea urchin-associated microbiota and their predicted chemical-defense-related functional potential remain poorly understood under aquaculture conditions. In this study, 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing was used to characterize microbial communities in rearing water, coelomic fluid, intestine, stomach contents, and surface mucus of Hemicentrotus pulcherrimus (H. pulcherrimus). KEGG Ortholo
papers.summary: This study characterizes the microbial communities associated with different body compartments of the sea urchin Hemicentrotus pulcherrimus under aquaculture conditions, using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. The authors find distinct microbial compositions across microhabitats and predict compartment-specific functional potentials related to chemical defense, suggesting that host-associated microbiota may play roles in ecological interactions and defense.

papers.title: Antibiotic Resistance Profiles of Bacterial Strains Isolated from the Roots, Cladodes and Rhizosphere of Opuntia dillenii (KerGawl.) Haw (Cactaceae) in the Coastal Zone of Benin.
papers.abstract: Endophytic and rhizosphere bacteria have considerable potential as bioinoculants for enhancing plant growth and improving soil health. However, despite their agricultural importance, their antibiotic resistance profiles remain poorly documented. This study assessed the antibiotic resistance of 31 bacterial strains isolated from the roots, cladodes, and rhizosphere of O. dillenii growing in the coastal zone of Benin. Antibiotic susceptibility was evaluated using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method according to CA-SFM/EUCAST guidelines. Depending on the bacterial genus, each strain was tested
papers.summary: This study characterized the antibiotic resistance profiles of 31 bacterial strains isolated from the roots, cladodes, and rhizosphere of Opuntia dillenii in Benin, using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method. The findings provide baseline data on antibiotic resistance in plant-associated bacteria, which is important for assessing the safety and efficacy of potential bioinoculants.

papers.title: Habitat-Dependent Ecological Differentiation of Soil and Water Microbiomes in High-Altitude Alpine Meadow Ecosystems on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau.
papers.abstract: High-altitude ecosystems are characterized by extreme environmental conditions that strongly influence microbial community structure and function. However, whether soil and water microbiomes exhibit similar ecological responses to environmental variation in alpine meadow ecosystems on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau remains poorly understood. Here, we combined 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metagenomic sequencing to compare soil and water microbiomes across two regions (LZ and NQ) with distinct physicochemical profiles. Environmental heterogeneity was more pronounced in water habitats, wher
papers.summary: This study compares soil and water microbiomes in high-altitude alpine meadows on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau using 16S rRNA gene amplicon and metagenomic sequencing. It finds that environmental heterogeneity is more pronounced in water habitats, leading to distinct ecological differentiation between soil and water microbial communities.

papers.title: Metagenomic Insights into the Seasonal Distribution and Dissemination Risks of Biocide and Metal Resistance Genes in a Subtropical Coastal Ecosystem.
papers.abstract: The widespread use of antimicrobial biocides and metals has led to the continuous accumulation of biocide and metal resistance genes (BMRGs) in the environment. The issue is of growing concern, as it reduces the efficacy of these agents and poses a potential threat to coastal ecological security. However, the extent of coastal BMRG pollution, its transmission mechanisms, and the influence of seasonal variations on its assembly remain poorly understood. In this study, metagenomic sequencing was employed to investigate BMRGs, microbiomes, and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) within the subtropical
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to examine the seasonal distribution and dissemination risks of biocide and metal resistance genes (BMRGs) in a subtropical coastal ecosystem. The findings reveal how BMRGs are influenced by seasonal variations and mobile genetic elements, highlighting potential risks to coastal ecological security.

papers.title: Establishment of an in vitro aerobic bacterial community as a model of the human lung microbiome.
papers.abstract: The human lung microbiome is increasingly recognized as a key player in drug metabolism, yet it remains largely understudied. To replicate this complex physiological environment in a controlled setting, we developed a simplified artificial lung microbiome model composed of four representative bacterial species: Pseudomonas koreensis, Rothia aeria, Neisseria cinerea, and Streptococcus downei. We successfully established a stable 10-day co-culture at 34°C using brain heart infusion medium, as validated by quantitative PCR, viability PCR, and conventional microbiological methodologies. Integrated
papers.summary: This study establishes a simplified in vitro aerobic bacterial community model of the human lung microbiome using four representative species, maintaining stability over 10 days in co-culture. The model provides a controlled system to study lung microbiome dynamics and drug metabolism, addressing a gap in current research tools.

papers.title: Characterizing the parvovirome of Swazi bats: novel species, highly divergent lineages, endogenous viral elements, and taxonomic challenges.
papers.abstract: Parvoviridae (small, nonenveloped ssDNA viruses) currently includes 281 species in two vertebrate- and four invertebrate-infecting subfamilies. While parvovirus-derived sequences are frequently identified in viromes, their taxonomy and host affiliation can be challenging due to high host and genetic diversity. We investigated the faecal parvovirome of 46 bats (7 insectivorous and 1 frugivorous species) from Eswatini and identified 28 novel viral species in 29 individuals (63.0%). The majority of these (22/28, 78.6%) belonged to nine genera (including two that are previously undescribed) within
papers.summary: This study characterizes the parvovirus diversity in fecal samples from 46 bats in Eswatini, identifying 28 novel viral species, including two previously undescribed genera and highly divergent lineages. The findings highlight the vast genetic diversity of parvoviruses in bats and the challenges this poses for taxonomy and host assignment.

papers.title: Dynamics of archaeal diversity and functionality in the piglet gut microbiome under common antimicrobial treatments.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota comprises a diverse and dynamic community of microorganisms that collectively enhance host metabolism, physiology, and overall functionality. In this context, the swine archaeome remains largely underexplored despite growing evidence that archaea may greatly influence host health. Advances in high-throughput approaches provide new opportunities to reveal the dynamics and composition of archaea. Herein, we uncover the taxonomic and functional landscape of the piglet archaeome during the weaning transition under multiple experimental conditions, integrating shotgun metagenomic
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study characterizes the archaeal community (archaeome) in the piglet gut microbiome during weaning and under different antimicrobial treatments, using shotgun metagenomics. It reveals the taxonomic and functional dynamics of archaea, highlighting their potential role in gut health and response to antimicrobial exposure.

papers.title: Long-reads metagenomics reveals the effects of dulse supplementation on the poultry caecal bacteriome and its associated genetic repertoire.
papers.abstract: Dulse (Palmaria palmata) is a macroalgal feed ingredient rich in polysaccharides and bioactive compounds that offers a sustainable strategy to enhance animal health and productivity through modulation of gut microbiota. However, the impact of dulse supplementation on the taxonomic composition and genetic repertoire of the broiler chicken caecal microbiota remains poorly characterised.
papers.summary: This study uses long-read metagenomics to investigate how supplementing broiler chicken feed with dulse (a red macroalga) affects the caecal microbiome and its functional genetic content. The findings reveal changes in the bacteriome composition and associated genetic repertoire, suggesting that dulse may modulate gut health in poultry.

papers.title: Shotgun metagenomic analysis reveals taxonomic and functional alterations in the gut microbiome across prodromal and symptomatic Lewy body disease.
papers.abstract: Lewy body disease (LBD) is a progressive neurodegenerative a-synucleinopathy, whereas isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is recognized as a prodromal stage of LBD. Although growing evidence implicates the gut-brain axis in neurodegeneration, the taxonomic and functional roles of the gut microbiome across the prodromal-to-symptomatic LBD continuum remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics to characterize gut microbiome taxonomic and functional changes across the prodromal (iRBD) and symptomatic stages of Lewy body disease, revealing distinct microbial alterations along the disease continuum. The findings support a role for the gut-brain axis in LBD progression and identify potential microbiome-based biomarkers for early detection.

papers.title: GUT MICROBIOTA ALTERATIONS IN RODENT MODELS OF CHOLESTASIS INDUCED BY BILE DUCT LIGATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW.
papers.abstract: Cholestatic liver diseases are a major public health issue, marked by impaired bile flow and significant disruptions in liver and systemic physiology. Growing evidence points to the gut microbiota as a key player in cholestasis pathogenesis through gut-liver axis interactions. This systematic review aimed to synthesize and evaluate current findings on intestinal microbiota changes in rodents (rats and mice) subjected to bile duct ligation (BDL)-induced cholestasis, focusing on microbial diversity, taxonomic shifts, and potential pathophysiological implications.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence from rodent studies on how bile duct ligation-induced cholestasis alters gut microbiota composition, revealing consistent shifts in microbial diversity and specific taxa. These changes may contribute to cholestasis pathophysiology through the gut-liver axis, highlighting the microbiota as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: From diversity to function: microbiome-mediated plant growth promotion, secondary metabolism, and antimicrobial resistance in Rauwolfia serpentina.
papers.abstract: This study presents the first metagenomic analysis of the root and rhizosphere microbiomes of Rauvolfia serpentina, an endangered medicinal plant. Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the diverse microbial communities and their functional attributes to assess the ecological and biotechnological potential of this plant-associated microbiome.
papers.summary: This study provides the first metagenomic analysis of the root and rhizosphere microbiomes of the endangered medicinal plant Rauwolfia serpentina, revealing the diversity and functional potential of its associated microbial communities. The findings highlight roles in plant growth promotion, secondary metabolism, and antimicrobial resistance, offering insights into the ecological and biotechnological significance of this plant's microbiome.

papers.title: Day-21 gut microbiota community state types are associated with bronchopulmonary dysplasia classification in preterm infants: a pilot shotgun metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a major complication in preterm infants, and its clinical classification remains strongly influenced by gestational maturity and the evolving respiratory course. In this exploratory study, we investigated whether early-life gut microbiota configurations at postnatal day 21 are associated with subsequent formal BPD classification at 36 weeks postmenstrual age and whether they provide ecological information relevant to preterm infant microbiome development.
papers.summary: This pilot study in preterm infants found that the composition of gut microbiota at postnatal day 21 is associated with the later classification of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) at 36 weeks postmenstrual age. The findings suggest that early-life gut microbial community states may offer ecological insights relevant to preterm infant development and BPD risk.

papers.title: A realistic simulation-based benchmark of microbiome normalization in sample stratification and taxa-level analysis.
papers.abstract: Normalization is a critical step in microbiome studies because sequencing depth and sparsity can strongly affect downstream analyses. In real datasets, however, the underlying biological signal is unknown, making it difficult to determine whether a normalization method preserves true group differences or introduces distortions. To address this problem in a way that remains relevant to real applications, we developed a simulation-based evaluation framework informed by real microbiome data. The framework generates realistic datasets with known ground truth and enables quantitative comparison of
papers.summary: This paper presents a simulation-based benchmark framework for evaluating microbiome normalization methods, using realistic data with known ground truth to assess their performance in sample stratification and taxa-level analysis. The framework addresses the challenge of unknown biological signals in real datasets, providing a quantitative comparison of normalization approaches.

papers.title: Cigarette Butts as an Emerging Urban Habitat Driving Microbial Niche Differentiation.
papers.abstract: Cigarette butts are common yet overlooked pollutants in urban environments. How this anthropogenic niche shapes microbial life-history strategies and evolutionary mechanisms remains poorly understood, limiting assessments of microbial adaption and urban ecosystem health. However, systematic and multiscale evidence on the ecological effects of cigarette butts on microbial communities remains scarce. Here, we collected cigarette butts, litter, and soil samples from urban parks in 35 Chinese cities and integrated third-generation 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing, metagenomics, and transcriptomics to
papers.summary: This study investigates cigarette butts as a novel anthropogenic habitat for microbes, using multi-omics (16S rRNA, metagenomics, transcriptomics) on samples from 35 Chinese cities. It reveals that cigarette butts drive microbial niche differentiation, shaping distinct life-history strategies and evolutionary adaptations in urban environments. The findings highlight the ecological impact of a common pollutant on microbial communities and urban ecosystem health.

papers.title: Functional signatures of the gut microbiome in middle-aged regular runners: insights from a metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Exercise influences host metabolism and inflammation, but its functional effects on the gut microbiome in middle-aged populations remain unclear. This study used shotgun metagenomics to investigate the associations between long-term endurance running and the gut microbial ecosystem and its functional potential in middle-aged adults.
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the gut microbiome of middle-aged regular runners with that of non-runners, revealing distinct functional signatures associated with endurance exercise. The findings suggest that long-term running is linked to specific microbial metabolic pathways that may influence host metabolism and inflammation, providing insights into how exercise shapes the gut ecosystem in middle-aged adults.

papers.title: Magnolia biondii-Derived Exosome-Like Nanoparticles Ameliorate Ulcerative Colitis by Suppressing Inflammation, Reducing Oxidative Stress, and Modulating Gut Microbiota.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory bowel disease with limited treatment options and suboptimal remission rates. Plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles have emerged as promising therapeutic agents due to their natural origin, biocompatibility, and capacity to deliver bioactive cargo. This study aimed to isolate exosome-like nanoparticles from the decoction of Magnolia biondii flower buds (Xinyi) (MFELNs) and evaluate their therapeutic potential in a murine model of UC.
papers.summary: This study isolated exosome-like nanoparticles from Magnolia biondii flower buds and tested them in a mouse model of ulcerative colitis. The nanoparticles reduced inflammation and oxidative stress while modulating gut microbiota, suggesting a potential natural therapeutic approach for UC.

papers.title: Enterococcus faecium pneumonia diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing in a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
papers.abstract: Enterococcus faecium is a rare pathogen in community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), and its diagnosis is challenging, particularly when prior antibiotic therapy hampers isolation by conventional culture. We report a 72-year-old man with a 6-year history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who presented with fever, cough, and progressive dyspnea. Despite empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam followed by imipenem-cilastatin), his condition deteriorated into acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. All routine cultures of
papers.summary: This case report describes a rare instance of Enterococcus faecium pneumonia in a COPD patient, diagnosed via metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) after conventional cultures failed due to prior antibiotic use. It highlights the utility of mNGS for identifying uncommon pathogens in complex respiratory infections, especially when standard diagnostics are inconclusive.

papers.title: Diversity and taxonomic differences in the oral microbiota of stroke patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: In recent years, a growing body of evidence suggests that stroke may be associated with an imbalance in the oral microbiome. To further elucidate this potential link, this study aims to systematically compare differences in the oral microbiome between stroke patients and healthy individuals.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis compares the oral microbiome of stroke patients with healthy controls, finding significant differences in microbial diversity and taxonomic composition. The results support a potential link between oral microbiota imbalance and stroke, highlighting specific bacterial taxa that may be associated with the condition.

papers.title: Global research landscape and trends of metabolomics in diabetic kidney disease: focus on immunometabolic interactions.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a devastating microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus, arises from intricate crosstalk between metabolic disorders and immune dysregulation. Metabolomics has emerged as a powerful tool to unravel the immunometabolic mechanisms underlying DKD, facilitating early disease diagnosis, mechanistic pathway interpretation, and therapeutic biomarker discovery. This study aimed to systematically delineate the global research landscape and evolutionary trends of DKD metabolomics, with a key emphasis on immunometabolic interactions.
papers.journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare
papers.summary: This paper provides a systematic bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape and trends in metabolomics applied to diabetic kidney disease (DKD), with a specific focus on immunometabolic interactions. It maps the evolution of the field, identifies key research themes, and highlights the growing role of metabolomics in uncovering disease mechanisms and discovering biomarkers.

papers.title: Optimized protocol for profiling mucosa-associated microbiota from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded gut tissues from treatment-naïve pediatric patients with Crohn's disease.
papers.abstract: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues are yet underutilized resources for microbiome studies. Data on the mucosa-associated microbiota (MAM) of patients with Crohn's disease (CD) are scarce, due to several methodological limitations. In this study, we aimed to develop and validate a new optimized amplicon-based workflow to profile MAM from FFPE gut biopsies of pediatric CD patients.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study presents a new optimized amplicon-based workflow for profiling mucosa-associated microbiota from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) gut biopsies, addressing methodological limitations that have hindered microbiome studies using these valuable archived tissues. The protocol was validated on treatment-naïve pediatric Crohn's disease patients, enabling reliable microbial profiling from FFPE samples and potentially expanding the utility of biobanked tissues for microbiome research.

papers.title: Urinary Microbiota in Female Patients With Dry and Wet Overactive Bladder (OAB).
papers.abstract: This study is aimed at comparing the urinary microbiota between OAB patients and healthy controls and at assessing whether urinary incontinence status affects the urinary microbiota in OAB patients.
papers.summary: This study compares the urinary microbiota of female patients with overactive bladder (OAB) to healthy controls, and further examines differences between those with dry and wet OAB. The findings reveal distinct microbial profiles associated with OAB and its subtypes, suggesting that urinary microbiota may play a role in the pathophysiology of OAB.

papers.title: Paired comparison of tumor core and airway lumen (BALF) microbiomes in lung adenocarcinoma: deciphering specific Bacillus enrichment and immunomodulation.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading cause of cancer mortality. While the lung microbiome influences tumorigenesis, the spatial heterogeneity between the airway reservoir (bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, BALF) and the actual intratumoral niche remains underexplored. Understanding this distinction is critical for identifying true tumor-resident drivers.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study compares the microbiomes of tumor core tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) from lung adenocarcinoma patients, revealing spatial heterogeneity and a specific enrichment of Bacillus in the tumor core. The findings suggest that Bacillus may play a role in tumor immunomodulation, highlighting the importance of distinguishing true tumor-resident microbes from airway contaminants.

papers.title: Gut microbiota profiles in pediatric atopic dermatitis and their relationship with skin microbiota: an Indonesian case-control study.
papers.abstract: The bacterial gut microbiota has been implicated in the pathophysiology of atopic dermatitis (AD), yet most studies have focused on Western populations and have typically examined the gut or skin microbiota in isolation. Evidence for interactions between skin and gut microbiota in inflammatory skin diseases remains limited, particularly in pediatric cohorts from non-Western settings. Here, we profiled the bacterial gut microbiota in children with AD from Indonesia, and evaluated the relationship with bacterial skin microbiota using paired gut and skin samples from the same individuals.
papers.summary: This study profiles the gut microbiota of Indonesian children with atopic dermatitis and compares it with their skin microbiota using paired samples, finding associations between the two microbial communities. It provides new evidence from a non-Western pediatric population, highlighting potential gut-skin microbiome interactions in AD.
